flashcards.q: What is the softmax-with-temperature formula, and what happens at the T=0 and T->inf limits?
flashcards.a: p_i = exp(z_i/T) / sum(exp(z_j/T)); T->0 collapses to argmax (greedy); T->inf flattens toward uniform distribution.

flashcards.q: What is top-p (nucleus) sampling's specific failure mode that motivated min-p?
flashcards.a: At confident steps, reaching a fixed cumulative probability threshold can still require admitting a long tail of individually near-irrelevant tokens.

flashcards.q: How is the min-p inclusion threshold computed?
flashcards.a: threshold = min_p * P(top-1 token) -- it scales with the model's own confidence at that step, unlike fixed top-k/top-p thresholds.

flashcards.q: Why is beam search the wrong default for open-ended generation despite maximizing sequence probability?
flashcards.a: Holtzman et al. (2019) showed human text lives in the 'typical set,' not the probability-maximizing mode; beam search's success at maximizing joint probability is exactly why its output reads as bland and repetitive.

flashcards.q: Distinguish frequency penalty from presence penalty.
flashcards.a: Frequency penalty scales with how many times a token has already appeared; presence penalty is a flat penalty applied for any prior occurrence regardless of count.

flashcards.q: What is the speculative decoding accept/reject rule and why does it preserve exactness?
flashcards.a: Accept a draft token with probability min(1, p_target/p_draft); on rejection, resample from the residual distribution max(p_target - p_draft, 0), normalized -- this makes the output distribution provably identical to sampling the target model alone.

flashcards.q: What acceptance rate does EAGLE-3 achieve on coding/instruction-following tasks, and what architectural trick gets it there?
flashcards.a: 0.80-0.88 acceptance, achieved by training the draft head on the target model's fused internal features across layers rather than raw token embeddings.

flashcards.q: What production latency/cost gains are reported for EAGLE-3-class speculative decoding in 2026?
flashcards.a: Roughly 2.8x latency reduction and about 47% inference cost reduction in reported production benchmarks.

flashcards.q: What does constrained decoding guarantee, and what does it NOT guarantee?
flashcards.a: It guarantees syntactic validity (the output always parses against the grammar/schema) by masking invalid tokens to -inf logit; it does not guarantee semantic correctness.

flashcards.q: What is XGrammar and what per-token overhead does it add?
flashcards.a: The default structured-generation grammar backend in vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM as of 2026, adding under 40 microseconds per token, negligible vs the model's 10-50ms/token inference cost.

flashcards.q: Why does beam search need repetition penalties more than sampling-based decoding does?
flashcards.a: Once a repeated phrase enters a high-joint-probability beam, continuing it can be locally probability-maximizing; penalties are most effective at flattening this feedback loop early, before it entrenches.

flashcards.q: Is min-p settled as superior to top-p in the research community?
flashcards.a: No -- a 2025 critique (Schaeffer et al.) argues the ICLR 2025 benchmarks showing min-p's advantage contain evaluation artifacts; the debate is unresolved as of 2026.
